test_title: PYST 16: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: If a shopkeeper sells sugar at ₹44.8 per kg, he is able to make a 12% profit. Due to water seepage, (1)/(5) of the sugar is damaged. What should now be the selling price per kg of the rest of the sugar to have a 5% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) per kg = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit%) = 44.8 ÷ 1.12 = ₹40.

To gain a 5% overall profit, the target revenue per kg of initial stock must be 40 × 1.05 = ₹42.

Since 1/5 of the sugar is damaged, only 4/5 of the quantity remains to be sold.

The entire target revenue must be generated by the remaining sugar.

New Selling Price per kg = Target Revenue ÷ Remaining Fraction = 42 ÷ (4/5) = 42 × 5 ÷ 4 = ₹52.5.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹52.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of sugar = ₹44.8 per kg

Initial profit = 12%

Damaged portion = 1/5 of the total sugar

Target overall profit = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit/100)

Total Selling Price = Total Cost Price × (1 + Desired Profit/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2241c1aa01475eea70b15f2d20773d8276e3c35e993591877c2cf14ffd96229.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total quantity of sugar be 5 kg.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) per kg = 44.8 ÷ 1.12 = ₹40

⇒ Total CP for 5 kg = 5 × 40 = ₹200

⇒ Since 5% overall profit is required, target Total SP = 200 × 1.05 = ₹210

⇒ Quantity of damaged sugar = 1/5 of 5 kg = 1 kg (yields ₹0 revenue)

⇒ Remaining quantity to be sold = 5 − 1 = 4 kg

⇒ New Selling Price per kg = Target Total SP ÷ Remaining Quantity

⇒ New SP per kg = 210 ÷ 4 = ₹52.5

**∴ The correct answer is ₹52.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Selling Price Relation

When profit is made, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100. For loss, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Impact of Damaged Goods on Profit

Goods that are completely damaged yield zero revenue. This effectively acts as a 100% loss on that specific portion, meaning the remaining goods must be sold at a higher markup to achieve the target overall profit.

Weighted Average in Profit & Loss

If quantity is split into parts (e.g., Q₁ and Q₂) sold at profit % P₁ and P₂, overall profit % = (Q₁P₁ + Q₂P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂). For completely damaged goods, P = −100%.
